_comment: The operating point the verifier's own training loop runs at, bound as bytes instead of left implicit. This file exists because the delivered bundle bound TWO incompatible things and reconciled them nowhere: task.toml [metadata.optimization] binds budget_hours = 0.12 h as the per-attempt completion bound and tests/checkers.py check_bound_envelope_respected GRADES that bound, while environment/shape.json bound an operating point at which a single attempt is measured at 7.59 h and cannot execute one optimizer step inside an 80 GB H100. A verifier that grades a bound it also violates can never award its own full reward. Both points are carried here, named, with the evidence for each.
selected_reason: The demonstration point is the point solution/TRUTH.md already declares the reference is demonstrated at: 'the reference is demonstrated end to end at the fixture shape only'. It is selected by default because it is the only delivered point at which the oracle can reach the bound full reward inside the bound envelope. The bound point stays reachable by name and stays carried as the gap it already was.

verifier_robustness._comment: trinity/FORGE.md Phase 0 item 9f binds these four by name. seed/contract.yaml carries all four as 'conservative default, carried by name' with no number, and nothing in the delivered bundle bound one either. These are the numbers this slot binds, each derived from a value the bundle's own bytes already bind rather than invented here.
verifier_robustness.window_ceiling_source: task.toml [metadata.optimization].budget_hours = 0.12 h, whose bound role is 'per-attempt completion bound'. 0.12 * 3600 = 432 s. This is the tightest window the delivered bytes bind and tests/checkers.py check_bound_envelope_respected already grades it, so it is the ceiling a completing attempt must sit inside.
verifier_robustness.session_ceiling_source: task.toml [metadata.optimization].max_timeout_hours = 6.0 h, whose bound role is 'refinement-loop terminator across attempts'. Never an alias of budget_hours.
verifier_robustness.load_profile: one verifier process, one accelerator or none, no concurrent graded session on the same device
verifier_robustness.score_stability_requirement: seed/contract.yaml supersedes identical-score with verdict stability, because same-seed GPU re-execution does not reproduce on this workload. The demonstration point pins device to cpu precisely so that the stronger identical-score property is recoverable here: no kernel nondeterminism is in the graded path at this point.

demonstration._comment: Real, runnable, and graded. Not synthetic: the verifier trains and evaluates here exactly as it would at the bound point, through the same tests/train_eval.py, the same tests/frozen_gpt.py and the same tests/bia_optim.py. What changes is the size of the substrate, not one line of the graded arithmetic, not one of the ten checkers, not the reward formula and not the consolidation rules. eval_stride, sustain_window, max_steps and target_loss are carried unchanged from the shape the delivered tests/fixtures/ were compiled at, so this point IS the fixture shape made executable.
demonstration.device_reason: Pinned so the graded number is reproducible on any host and identical across stability_trials. seed/contract.yaml records that this workload's same-seed spread on GPU is the same order as its seed-to-seed sigma; pinning cpu removes that source from the graded path entirely rather than tolerating it.

anchors.authority: tests/fixtures/accept_reference_session.json anchors block, which the delivered bundle already compiled at baseline_metric 500, target_metric 150, target_loss 1.75. These are NOT the upstream record anchors 3250 and 2690; a step count is only meaningful against the operating point that produced it, so the upstream anchors travel with the bound point and these travel with this one. Carried under gap-oer-scaled-operating-point-unmeasured, exactly as solution/TRUTH.md already carries it.

bound._comment: The H100 operating point environment/shape.json binds. Carried, named, and NOT selected, because it is measured unrunnable. Kept reachable by BIA_OPERATING_POINT=bound so the gap is a gap and not a deletion.

measured_evidence.single_optimizer_step_method: tests/frozen_gpt.py forward+backward at 8 of the 512 bound sequences on an idle NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, scaled to the bound 512-sequence step
measured_evidence.oom_evidence: tests/train_eval.py line 131 raises torch.OutOfMemoryError on the FIRST optimizer step on an idle 80 GB H100: the un-microbatched forward over 512x1024 positions materializes a 512x1024x4096 fp32 logits tensor of 8.59 GB plus cross-entropy intermediates, reaching 76.91 GiB allocated before failing to allocate a further 4.50 GiB. Microbatching is not available as a remedy: grad_accum and micro_steps are frozen_axis_keys in tests/recipe_schema.json and tests/checkers.py check_frozen_axes_untouched grades forward_passes_per_step == 1.
measured_evidence.substrate_prologue_method: tests/bia_data.py markov_stream is a Python-level loop measured at 1.50 microseconds per token, over stream_tokens_train = 268435456

shape.operating_point_state: unmeasured on the bound envelope, carried under gap-oer-scaled-operating-point-unmeasured
